relationshipToReleaseCapabilities: ADDITIVE. GET /release/capabilities serves RELEASE_CAPABILITIES_R8_3.3 (asOf 2026-08-26) with a four-state vocabulary (ENABLED / LIMITED / DISABLED / EXPERIMENTAL_INTERNAL). That registry is the SERVER's statement about itself and is not replaced. This registry is the PRODUCT's statement about what v1 ships, in the five-state vocabulary NEW3 was asked for, and every row names the runtime row it derives from. Where the two disagree, the runtime registry wins on fact and this one wins on shipping decision. R13 NOTE: GET /release/capabilities still serves NO platform dimension - observed 30 Aug, the string "platform" appears nowhere in its 24-row payload. The per-platform truth therefore lives HERE and is enforced at review time, not at runtime, until CCR-2026-08-30-04 lands.

stateVocabulary.ENABLED_V1: Ships in v1, to every user, with the stated coverage and the stated uncertainty rendered.
stateVocabulary.INTERNAL_EXPERIMENTAL: Runs, is measured, is never reachable by a user in v1. No public surface, no marketing claim.
stateVocabulary.DISABLED_NOT_READY: The gap is OURS — code, coverage, or an unmeasured property. Closing it is our work.
stateVocabulary.DISABLED_EXTERNAL_BLOCK: The gap is NOT ours — an authorization, a credential, a registrar's answer. No amount of our work closes it.
stateVocabulary.POST_V1: Deliberately out of v1 scope. Not a gap.
stateVocabulary.ENABLED_V1_KILLABLE: Ships in v1 on this platform, AND carries a capability kill switch that can disable it on this platform alone without disabling the capabilities named in `mustNotDisable`. Used where a platform policy risk is real but unproven.
stateVocabulary.UNKNOWN_PENDING_FOUNDER: The platform itself is contested between two binding documents. Not ENABLED, not DISABLED, not POST_V1. No claim may be made about this capability on this platform in either direction, and no work is scheduled against it, until the founder settles the surface. See `platformStatus.web`.

A party name carrying a distinguishing token resolves: 'SATENDER KUMAR ANTIL' returns 3 results with the authority at RANK 1 in 295.6 ms, degraded absent. A party name built only of corpus-common tokens still refuses: 'SANJAY KUMAR MISHRA @ SANJAY MISHRA' returns 0 with degraded=[sparse_unbounded], emptyBecause=query_too_broad_to_rank, rarestDf 0.0654, and pays 1,239.2 ms to get there.

capabilities.coverageDefinition: MEASURED across six narrowing scopes of one query ('bail'). ADMITTED: one named court + 3 days -> 5 results in 154.6 ms; one named court + 1 month -> 5 results in 418.1 ms. REFUSED: one named court + 8 months; courts:[hc] category + 1 month at 262.6 ms; courts:[hc] + 29 days at 207.4 ms; unfiltered at 2.9 ms. Narrow control 'anticipatory bail cheque dishonour' + courts:[hc] + 29 days -> 5 results in 78.8 ms.
capabilities.whyNotReady: READ FROM THE CODE, not inferred: services/api/src/search/retrieve.ts computes rarestDf from lexeme_document_frequency and refuses when rarestDf > SPARSE_MAX_RANKED_DOCUMENT_FREQUENCY (0.05, ~935,000 documents). `filters` is a parameter of that same function and is NOT consulted before the refusal. The bound is therefore corpus-wide while the query is not. An advocate who has already narrowed to one court and one month is told their query is too broad — which is the daily-loop case, and the one where narrowing is exactly what they did.
